subject: Elevated 5xx/429 + retry storm — request for credits and immediate mitigation
messages:
From: Tim Sato <ops@orthomed.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: High 5xx/429 rate + retry storm hitting checkout (URGENT)

Rachel / Neha —

We started seeing an elevated rate of 5xx and 429 responses from your API around 15:05 PDT today. Our payment checkout saw repeated timeouts and many of our customers got checkout failures; our retry logic triggered a retry storm which made the errors worse. Attached are sample logs and a short span from our tracing showing ~2.3k failed requests in a 9 minute window.

Impact: ~1,200 failed transactions that required manual follow-up; peak latency spiked to 3.4s for successful responses right after the failures. This is a production outage for our checkout flow.

We need three things immediately:
- Immediate mitigation (pause automatic retries at your edge / route our traffic to a stable model variant)
- Root cause and ETA for full remediation
- Compensation for the incident — this event looks like an SLA breach, please propose credits and any operational steps you will take to prevent recurrence.

Attaching logs: orthomed-retry-logs-2026-04-09.zip

Tim Sato
Head of Ops, OrthoMed Inc
ops@orthomed.com


From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Sato <ops@orthomed.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, ethan_park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rate + retry storm hitting checkout (URGENT)

Tim —

Thanks for the quick flag and for the logs. I’m sorry for the disruption and I’ve looped in Monica (CS) and Markus (Engineering) to lead the mitigation and root cause. Ethan is on standby for any executive escalations.

Immediate actions we are taking now:
- Temporarily taking your production traffic off the autoscaled pool and routing to a dedicated, warmed pool (expected within 10 minutes).
- Disabling aggressive edge retries for your routes to avoid amplifying downstream errors.
- Collecting internal diagnostic traces; Markus will own the postmortem and ETA.

We’ll follow up in the next 20 minutes with a concrete ETA and a proposal for compensation. I’ll also share an incident link for visibility.

—
Rachel Kim

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, ethan_park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rate + retry storm hitting checkout (technical update)

Quick technical summary:
- What we observed: a sudden spike in backend queue depth triggered a cascade where the serving runtime returned 429s under backpressure; client-side retries then created a retry amplification loop leading to transient 5xx responses when queues exhausted.
- Root cause (initial): an autoscaler policy misconfiguration pushed more traffic into a smaller warm pool during a scheduled rebalancing window. That combined with your client retry behavior created the storm.
- Immediate mitigations performed (15:38 PDT):
  * Moved OrthoMed routes to a warmed, dedicated pool to stabilize latency.
  * Disabled aggressive server-side retries and backpressure-trapping at the edge.
  * Raised priority of any inflight requests for your account to avoid drop.
- Next steps: full postmortem scheduled; we will validate the autoscaler policy and update default protection (circuit breaker thresholds) to avoid the same amplification pattern. ETA for full remediation and code/config change: 48 hours.

I attached a short snippet of server error traces for traceability (server-errors-0429-snippet.txt).

—
Markus Klein
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Sato <ops@orthomed.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rate + retry storm hitting checkout (mitigation & credits proposal)

Tim —

Thank you for your patience while we stabilized the route. Per Markus’ note, routing you to a dedicated, warmed pool has brought error rates back to baseline. We understand this impacted checkout and customer experience — we propose the following immediate remediation and compensation package:

1) Operational remediation
- Confirmed: your route is on a dedicated warm pool and protective circuit-breakers have been tuned for your traffic pattern for the next 72 hours.
- Action: we will deliver a postmortem within 48 hours with root cause and the config change.

2) Compensation proposal (initial)
- Pro-rated credit for the window of degraded availability: calculated as 25% of the daily pro-rated fee for the impacted usage window (we’ve attached a worked example: proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx).
- One week of complimentary Dedicated capacity for OrthoMed to avoid risk during the remediation window.

If this is acceptable, we’ll draft an SLA amendment and credit note (DocuSign) for signature. If it’s not, please tell us what you have in mind and we’ll escalate to execs.

Proposed exec touch: 30-min sync tomorrow (Fri) at 10:30 PDT to review the postmortem and finalize credits. Are you available?

—
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai

From: Anya Rojas <anya.rojas@orthomed.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Sato <ops@orthomed.com>, procurement@orthomed.com
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rate + retry storm hitting checkout (mitigation & credits proposal)

Rachel —

Thanks for the fast mitigation and the worked example. We appreciate the one-week capacity offer, but given the scale of impact (1,200 failed transactions; material revenue and manual reconciliation cost), a 25% pro-rated credit and 1 week of capacity feels out of step with the disruption.

Specifically:
- We expect an SLA-class credit rather than a goodwill credit. The incident meets the SLA failure thresholds for the month given the duration and error rate spike. Our procurement and finance teams will need a formal SLA amendment that spells out the credit calculation and timelines for application to invoices.
- We also request a higher immediate credit proposal: 40% of the pro-rated daily fee for the impacted window + waiving the next invoice for dedicated capacity for 30 days.

Executive engagement: we would like an exec-level call (SVP/VP) to discuss reconciliation and draw a path to prevent recurrence. Please confirm availability for a call tomorrow.

Regards,
Anya Rojas
Director, Platform Ops
Anya.Rojas@orthomed.com

(attachment referenced: reconciliation-summary.xlsx)

As a follow-up:
- Exec call: Fri, Apr 10 at 11:45 PDT (30 minutes) — Ethan, Monica and Markus will join. Please confirm if that works for your execs; we can shift as needed.
- Updated compensation offer (executive escalation): 20% credit of the monthly invoice prorated to the impacted window, plus a 30-day waiver for dedicated capacity charges for the next billing cycle. We are prepared to formalize via an SLA amendment and credit memo within 48 hours of the call.

If you need a larger proposal, Ethan will be empowered to approve additional credits on the call and note that we will prioritize the postmortem and delivery timeline.

Thanks again and we’ll see you on the call.
